text:
NOTICE OF PREPARATION AND SCOPING MEETING
                           West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss State Park
        Environmental Assessment or Environmental Impact Statement/Environmental Impact Report

Project Title:          West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss State Park

Project Proponent:      Tahoe Regional Planning Agency (TRPA)

Comment Period:         October 20, 2026 through November 20, 2026

Scoping Meeting:        November 2, 2026 in person in Tahoe City, CA See details below.

Lead Agencies:          TRPA and El Dorado County (County)
Contacts:               Rebecca Cremeen, Senior Planner                  Thea Graybill, Planning Manager
                        Tahoe Regional Planning Agency                   El Dorado County
                        Transportation Planning Department               Planning and Building Department
                        P.O. Box 5310                                    924 B Emerald Bay Rd
                        Stateline, NV 89449                              South Lake Tahoe, CA 96150
                        rcremeen@trpa.gov                                Thea.Graybill@edcgov.us

TRPA and the County are preparing a joint Environmental Assessment or Environmental Impact
Statement/Environmental Impact Report (EA or EIS /EIR) for the proposed West Shore Trail extension, a shared
use path that would connect Meeks Bay and D.L. Bliss State Park. The joint document will serve as either an EA
or an EIS prepared by TRPA in accordance with the TRPA Bi-State Compact, Code of Ordinances (Code), and
Rules of Procedure, and as an EIR prepared by the County in accordance with the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) and the State CEQA Guidelines. This section of trail was first contemplated and studied in
the State Route (SR) 89 Recreation Corridor Management Plan and Cascade to Meeks Trail Feasibility Study,
which can be accessed at: https://www.trpa.gov/rtp/sr-89-recreation-corridor-management-plan/.

The proposed shared use path crosses public lands, including National Forest System lands managed by the U.S.
Department of Agriculture Forest Service’s Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit (LTBMU), requiring compliance
with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). LTBMU will prepare separate NEPA documentation for the
project concurrent with preparation of the EA or EIS/EIR. The proposed project is partially located within
California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) highway right-of-way and on state lands managed by the
California Tahoe Conservancy (Conservancy) and California Department of Parks and Recreation (State Parks).
Caltrans, the Conservancy, and State Parks will serve as responsible agencies under CEQA.

This notice satisfies TRPA and CEQA requirements for a Notice of Preparation (NOP). Its purpose is to provide
public agencies, organizations, the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California, and interested members of the
public with sufficient information about the proposed project and its potential environmental effects to provide
meaningful input on the scope and content of the EA or EIS/EIR. A brief description of the project and its location
and the purpose and need for the project are provided below.

PROJECT LOCATION
The project site is in El Dorado County, California, on the West Shore of Lake Tahoe between Meeks Bay and
D.L. Bliss State Park, as shown in Figures 1 and 2. The proposed project consists of an approximately 6.5-mile
shared use path that would generally include a separated, 10-foot-wide paved path with 2-foot-wide shoulders.

Source: Adapted by Ascent in 2026.

Figure 1                      Regional Location Map

Source: Adapted by Ascent in 2026.

Figure 2          West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss Shared Use Path Alignments

PURPOSE AND NEED
The West Shore of Lake Tahoe is a highly visited recreation corridor, offering diverse opportunities to access
public lands and scenic views of Lake Tahoe. The SR89 Corridor Management Plan identifies keys goals and
coordinated strategies to reduce congestion, protect natural resources, and improve safety within the corridor.
The proposed 6.5 mile West Shore Trail extension, Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss State Park, advances the goals of the
SR89 Corridor Management Plan by extending the shared use bike and pedestrian path to connect key
recreation areas along the corridor.

The existing West Shore Trail currently spans approximately 12 miles and ends at Meeks Bay, leaving a critical
gap in the shared use path network for bicyclists, pedestrians, and other non-motorized users traveling south.
The proposed project would extend the trail approximately 6.5 miles to D.L. Bliss State Park, advancing the
regional vision for a continuous shared use path around Lake Tahoe, commonly referred to as the Tahoe Trail.
Completing the connection between Meeks Bay and D.L. Bliss State Park would improve connectivity between
destinations and provide an alternative to travel between recreation areas without a car.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The separated shared use path would be paved and generally designed to achieve a maximum grade of 8
percent. The path would also be designed to meet applicable accessibility and design standards, including the
U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service’s Outdoor Recreation and Trail Accessibility Guidelines and,
within Caltrans right-of-way, applicable Public Right-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines and Caltrans design
standards. Design exceptions may be necessary in some locations because of the steep slopes and challenging
terrain within the project corridor. The at-grade highway crossings would be designed to provide safe and
accessible crossings, with appropriate signage, pavement markings, and conflict-resolution measures,
consistent with applicable Caltrans design standards and requirements.

Two alignment alternatives for the proposed shared use path will be evaluated in the joint EA or EIS/EIR. Both
alignments, shown in Figure 2, would be located entirely on public land and would not require the use of private
property.

The proposed project would also include vista points that would serve as rest areas near the ends of steep
grades; highway crossings; and a transit stop and bus turnaround area along Lester Beach Road, with the
potential for a restroom and limited parking. The transit stop, restroom, and limited parking would be located
either near the SR 89 entrance to D.L. Bliss State Park or farther within the park near the campground entrance
kiosk.

The shared use path would connect to Meeks Bay to access the beach, campground, and resort. The section of
trail through Meeks Bay was evaluated separately as part of the Meeks Bay Restoration Project environmental
review.

Proposed Alignment

From the connection in Meeks Bay Resort, the proposed alignment would cross SR 89 through an undercrossing
and extend through the neighborhood south of Meeks Bay, generally on public lands north of and parallel to
Bayview Drive. An approximately 0.3-mile segment would be located on Bayview Drive and then Lakeview Drive,
where improvements would generally be limited to striping and signage. The alignment would cross Saturn
Drive before entering National Forest System lands.

From this location, the proposed alignment would use switchbacks to accommodate the steep terrain and meet
applicable trail grades. Near Sierra Drive, the alignment would transition to a location generally parallel to SR 89
and within Caltrans right-of-way on the mountainside of the highway. The alignment would continue south to

a point north of 2 Ring Road, where it would cross SR 89 at grade to the lakeside of the highway and would
continue south on the lakeside of SR 89.

The proposed alignment would then continue south, cross the portion of Lester Beach Road restricted to
authorized vehicle use, and extend through D.L. Bliss State Park closer to existing campground features while
maintaining a minimum 200-foot setback from individual campsites. The southern terminus would be located
along Lester Beach Road near the park entrance.

Alternative 1 Alignment

From the connection in Meeks Bay Resort, the Alternative 1 alignment would differ from the proposed
alignment primarily in the Meeks Bay and D.L. Bliss State Park areas. Near Meeks Bay, after crossing SR 89 with
an at-grade crossing, the Alternative 1 alignment would extend approximately 0.3 miles within Caltrans right-
of-way on the mountainside of and generally parallel to SR 89. It would then follow existing natural-surface
roads and cross public parcels, Saturn Drive, and Silvertip Court before converging with the proposed alignment.

The Alternative 1 alignment would coincide with the proposed alignment through the central portion of the
project corridor. Near D.L. Bliss State Park, however, it would remain on the mountain side of SR 89 farther
south before crossing the highway at grade at a location closer to D.L. Bliss State Park. Figure 2 shows the
Alternative 1 alignment crossing south of the proposed alignment crossing.

After crossing SR 89, the Alternative 1 alignment would continue through D.L. Bliss State Park, cross the portion
of Lester Beach Road restricted to authorized vehicle use, and pass north of Balancing Rock, generally closer to
SR 89 than the proposed alignment. It would then converge with the proposed alignment near the southern
terminus along Lester Beach Road.

Project Components Common to Both Alignment Alternatives

In addition to the shared use path itself, both action alternatives would include the following components:

    1. SR 89 highway crossings, with the southern crossing location varying by alignment;

    2. Bridges and/or boardwalks at Sierra Creek, Rubicon Creek, and other drainages;

    3. Retaining walls in areas of steep terrain, potentially located on one or both sides of the path and
       generally ranging from approximately 3 to 15 feet in height;

    4. Safety railings and other protective measures along path edges where retaining walls exceed 30 inches
       in height on the downhill side;

    5. Vista points that would also serve as rest areas;

    6. A transit stop and bus turnaround area, which could include a restroom and limited parking; and

    7. Other trail amenities, which could include interpretive signage, trash and recycling receptacles,
       benches, and bicycle racks.

EA OR EIS/EIR SCOPE
The EA or EIS/EIR will evaluate the direct and indirect significant and adverse environmental impacts of the
proposed project (i.e., the proposed West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss State Park). TRPA and the County
have determined that the EA or EIS/EIR shall evaluate potential environmental impacts in the following resource
areas:
    •   Aesthetics/Scenic Resources                           •   Agriculture and Forestry Resources

•   Air Quality                                             •   Land Use and Planning
    •   Biological Resources                                    •   Noise
    •   Cultural Resources                                      •   Population and Housing
    •   Energy                                                  •   Public Services and Utilities
    •   Geology, Soils, Land Capability, and Coverage           •   Recreation
    •   Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Climate Change             •   Transportation
    •   Hazards, Hazardous Materials, Human Health,             •   Tribal Cultural Resources
        and Risk of Upset                                       •   Utilities and Service Systems
    •   Hydrology and Water Quality                             •   Wildfire
In accordance with the TRPA Initial Environmental Checklist and State CEQA Guidelines Section 15130, the EA or
EIS/EIR will also include an analysis of cumulative impacts that considers the effects of the proposed project when
combined with the related effects of related past, present, and probable future projects in the surrounding area.

ALTERNATIVES
The EA or EIS/EIR will evaluate a range of alternatives to the proposed West Shore Trail alignment between Meeks
Bay and D.L. Bliss in accordance with the TRPA Rules of Procedure, Section 3.7.2 of the TRPA Code, and
Section 15126.6 of the State CEQA Guidelines. At a minimum, the EA or EIS/EIR will evaluate an action alternative,
including the Alternative 1 alignment shown in Figure 2 and described above, and the required no project
alternative. The no project alternative will reflect existing conditions at the time this NOP was published. TRPA
and the County have not yet determined whether additional alternatives to the proposed project will be evaluated
in the EA or EIS/EIR. Potential additional alternatives will be identified and considered based on scoping comments
and information developed during the environmental review process. Once selected, the alternatives will be
evaluated at a generally qualitative level of detail in the Draft EA or EIS/EIR and compared with the environmental
impacts of the proposed West Shore Trail alignment between Meeks Bay and D.L. Bliss State Park, consistent with
applicable TRPA and CEQA requirements. As part of the scoping process, TRPA and the County are seeking input
from interested stakeholders regarding potential alternatives for consideration in the EA or EIS/EIR.

PUBLIC REVIEW PERIOD
The NOP will be circulated for a 30-day public review period. Written comments on the scope and content of
the EIS/EIR may be submitted during the scoping period, beginning October 20, 2026, and ending at 5:00 p.m.
on November 20, 2026. Please submit written comments through the Comment Form on the TRPA website,
email to rcremeen@trpa.gov, or mailed to Rebecca Cremeen, Senior Planner, TRPA, at the address provided
above. Please include “West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss State Park EIS/EIR” in the subject line. Public
agencies submitting comments are requested to identify an agency contact person.

SCOPING MEETING
In addition to the opportunity to submit written comments, TRPA and the County will hold a public scoping
meeting near the project site to provide information about the proposed project, receive oral comments on the
scope and content of the EA or EIS/EIR, and answer general questions about the environmental review process.
The meeting will be held in person on November 2, 2026, as follows:

                  West Shore Trail – Meeks Bay to D.L. Bliss EA or EIS/EIR Scoping Meeting
                            November 2, 2026, Open House from 5:30-7:00 PM
                                      Tahoe City Public Utility District
                                            221 Fairway Drive
                                       Tahoe City, California 96145

The project will also be presented at the TRPA Advisory Planning Commission meeting on November 12, 2026.
The meeting will begin at 9:30 a.m. at 128 Market Street in Stateline, Nevada, with a virtual attendance option.

Because the project presentation is not time certain, participants should check the TRPA website one week before
the meeting for the agenda and virtual attendance information, which will be posted at the following location:
https://www.trpa.gov/meeting-materials. Public comments on the project may be provided during the public
interest comment period at the beginning and end of the meeting.
